card.law_is_about: A state-funded private-pension starting balance for children, with a collective default investment option.
card.they_want: Bind the collective investment strategy more tightly in the statute, including broad diversification, passive management and low costs.
card.they_claim: The government bill already requires the collective fund to invest exclusively in globally diversified stocks or stock funds.
card.the_problem: The addressed September government bill does not impose the stock-only requirement. That appeared in the earlier July consultation draft and was later restored in October.

locator.section: Article 1, proposed §24(3); §24(4) leaves asset classes to investment guidelines.

correction: The September government bill requires global diversification and the principles of return, security and liquidity; its §24(4) delegates eligible asset classes to guidelines. It does not require exclusive stock investment. The exact July 21 consultation version did impose that restriction, while the October 14 committee recommendation later restored an exclusive broad-global-stock rule. Neither is the government bill addressed at the October 5 hearing.
effect: The original government bill leaves more statutory investment discretion than described. Correcting that description strengthens, rather than defeats, the request to anchor additional investment safeguards directly in law.
limits: This is a narrow version-description slip. It does not show that the collective fund would actually invest in a particular non-equity asset, that a stock-only allocation is preferable, or that passive management and low costs follow automatically from that restriction. The rest of the requested safeguards remains a policy judgment. No intent is inferred.
context_and_alternatives: All 11 submission pages were read. The paragraph explicitly endorses the supposedly existing stock-only condition but immediately says it is insufficient; the request adds several separate investment principles. The broader reform position is not dependent on this descriptive slip.

A strong benign explanation is carry-over from the July consultation draft: the original 21 July 2026,15:48 version really contains the stock-only restriction. It was retrieved from a university-maintained public mirror after the ministry page failed. This explains the wording without making it correct for the later government bill.

The government memorandum physical 53 says a high share of stocks or stock funds is useful for education, but it does not convert the operative provision into an exclusive stock mandate. A policy intention is not the same as the described statutory restriction.

A later-amendment rescue was checked directly: committee recommendation BT 21/8606,14 October 2026, physical 29 shows the exact insertion against the original text. The submission is dated 22 September and its PDF creation metadata is 21 September, before that amendment. The later change is contextual corroboration, not silently substituted law.
The mirrored consultation draft’s provenance is explicit, and no byte-identical ministry copy is claimed. The finding itself rests on official original Bundestag submission and government-bill PDFs.
materiality_explanation: Minor: this overstates one existing constraint in a short investment-policy subsection; it does not alter the proposed public/default arrangement or undermine the separate requests for passive management, broad diversification and low costs.
direction_explanation: False narrowly: describing the bill as already imposing more binding investment limits understates the statutory gap. Correcting it gives greater support to the request for tighter investment safeguards. The preferred asset allocation itself is not adjudicated.
